heuristics: The walk is modelled as a random mapping on the r group elements (standard rho heuristic, Brent-Pollard correction for R-adding walks). The claim's success is 0.39, not the model's 0.675; the model is used only to choose the cap.

The 1.01 per-step price is an analytic instruction ledger: one dense Fp12 multiplication (the reference operation) plus 200 charged scalar instructions for the hash, table index, two 255-bit modular exponent updates, distinguished-point test, loop and cache-miss allowances.
A flat 2^31 reference-operation overhead is charged for the setup pairing, the 2^20-multiplier table, the 2^20 walk starts and verification; it is 2^-97 of the total.
Records store the exact 576-byte Fp12 element, not a fingerprint, so stored-key matches are true element matches and no false-match resolution is needed.
The success probability claimed is the rule threshold 0.39, well below the random-mapping model value 0.675 at the cap; it is not a confidence score.
limitations: Analytic complexity claim for a 2^128-step computation, not an executed attack; the rules allow an analytic argument.
Toy-scale experiment supports the mechanism and the collision-time heuristic at toy scope only, never a production complexity proof.

No group quotient is used: an earlier two-class inversion-quotient draft was withdrawn after review showed its transition is not a function on classes. The quotient saving (about 0.5 bits) is not claimed.
Peak storage is hard-capped at 2^79 bytes by an enforced capacity of 2^70 records (3.9x the design count) with a stop-inserting policy; memory does not enter this track's score.
